summary: Integrates speed/rate input channels over time to cumulative distance or higher-order accumulated values.
key_concepts: Speed CHOP converts rate-style input channels, such as speed in units per second, into cumulative distance-style output.
The first input is integrated by summing channel values per sample and dividing by the CHOP sample rate.
By default Speed CHOP is time-sliced, so it keeps adding or subtracting each cook frame.
Order selects first, second, or third order integration so velocity or acceleration can become position-like output.
When no input is connected, the Speed parameter generates a constant rate; that parameter is disabled once an input is connected.
The second input or Reset controls set the output to Reset Value, and While On reset holds that value until the reset input turns off.

key_params.name: order
key_params.note: First, second, or third order integration

key_params.name: speed
key_params.note: Generated speed when no input is connected

key_params.name: loop
key_params.note: Loop accumulated values across the Min/Max interval

key_params.name: zigzag
key_params.note: Mirror accumulated values inside the Min/Max interval

key_params.name: speedsamples
key_params.note: Apply speed per sample for multi-sample channels

key_params.name: offtoon
key_params.note: Reset when the reset input goes off to on

key_params.name: on
key_params.note: Reset and hold while the reset input is on

key_params.name: ontooff
key_params.note: Reset when the reset input goes on to off

common_gotchas: By default Speed CHOP is time-sliced and accumulates each cook frame.
Second input resets output when the reset channel condition is met.
When reset is held while-on, output holds the reset value until the reset input turns off.
Long-running values can become numerically large and step; Reset On Start avoids stale accumulation after project restart.
A connected input disables the Speed parameter's generated-speed role.
Use Slope CHOP for the inverse operation: position to speed or acceleration.
Second or third order integration can drift quickly if constants and reset behavior are not deliberate.
